comments.body:
Settled and delivered in builder PR #4 (head ed0cc01).

Brief: /world/architect/wiki/Brief.

Organization: poet (maker) writes poem.md; editor (judge) reads input and candidate, requests concrete revisions or approves the exact candidate; reader (user) reads each published release and reports clarity, flow, imagery, and fit. The contracts specify inputs, handoffs, judgment criteria, and norms without prescribing implementation.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
# PoemWorld: a three-role world that writes a short poem

Make a new domain for HuTian: PoemWorld, the smallest world that is still a whole world. From a request it writes a short poem, and the system releases the poem once it is approved.

What to make:

- A domain package `poemworld` (command `poemworld`, world id prefix `pw`) beside the seven domains under `src/`, added the way `DEV.md` says a domain is added: its definition through the `hutian.definitions` entry point, its organization graph in `assets/` in Chinese and English, its system and worker images, and its place in `install.sh`, the CI workflows and the per-domain checks.
- Three roles, one of each category a definition needs: `poet` makes the poem (`poem.md`) from the world's input; `editor` assesses it against the input, asks the poet for changes when it falls short, and approves each version; `reader` uses it: it reads each version the world publishes and says how the poem reads, which the poet and the editor watch. One edge, poet and editor. The release is the poem the editor approved last.
- Keep it small: the roles, their contracts and the release gate make it a world, not features.

Where it goes: one pull request to the private repository `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base branch `dev`, which holds HuTian's code. Merging it is the maintainer's decision after review.

How to try it: on `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted in a new directory, build its images there from that version (older images on the machine are not that version), run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh PoemWorld world with the input "Write a four-line poem about the first snow." to its release. The trial world's workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token that trial-machine's commands get as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2` (give their provider `auth` `claude-oauth` and `credential_env` `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2`), with at most 16 executions and 2000 model seconds: a simple task, a cheap worker and a small budget are enough to show the world works. The pull request says what was made and how the trial ended: the trial world's id, its release, and the poem.

issue.author: reviewer
issue.body:
I will accept a delivery only when it satisfies the frozen World objective for PoemWorld.

Acceptance standard:
- The builder delivery contains a complete poemworld domain package wired through the hutian.definitions entry point, with Chinese and English organization graphs, system/worker images, install.sh, CI workflows, and per-domain checks as required by DEV.md.
- The organization has exactly poet, editor, and reader with their stated functions, the poet-editor edge, contracts, and editor-owned release gate producing poem.md.
- For each offered version, the release pull request is cleanly mergeable, the package installs, the kernel reads the definition, and all regression checks pass; Docker-dependent checks must run on trial-machine.
- Before final approval, operator evidence must show a fresh trial installed the exact offered version, built images from it, ran the required input, and reached release. I will cross-check trial-machine status and trial-world records, including the released poem and world id.
- Diagnosis must reflect the actual trial and cover any supplied worlds/records, placing each issue in its proper layer and leaving no unresolved delivery or position problem. Worker-only shortcomings may remain only as a draft objective.

I will record the inspected commit, pull request, checks, trial world id/release/poem, and conclusion in this repository before approving release or final.
